# Slugs use underscores

Reported by a user: `slugify("Hello World")` returns `hello_world`. Slugs must use hyphens, and repeated or
surrounding spaces must not produce empty parts. `test_app.py` shows the expected output.
def slugify(title):
    """Turn a post title into a URL slug."""
    return title.lower().replace(" ", "_")
import unittest
from app import slugify


class T(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_slug(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Many   spaces here "), "many-spaces-here")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

content.text:
The bug is fixed: `slugify` in `app.py` now joins words with hyphens instead of underscores, and extra spaces no longer create empty parts. The test passes, and I didn't change `test_app.py`.

The new version is `"-".join(title.lower().split())`. Splitting on whitespace drops spaces at the start and end and collapses runs of spaces, so `"  Many   spaces here "` becomes `many-spaces-here`.

One thing outside the issue: punctuation isn't removed, so `"Hello, World!"` would give `hello,-world!`.
